reported.title: Debounce window too short (60 ms vs 40 ms requirement is fine, but 2 samples × 30 ms poll = 60 ms is OK) — actually the real bug: press during chime is lost
reported.description: When a press is confirmed while chiming, armed is set false but startChime is skipped; the press is silently dropped and the chime count is not incremented, so a press during the chime is ignored as required — but the button must be released before re-arming, which is correct. However the real defect: the 40 ms settle requirement is met only marginally and the 120 ms start latency is met, so this is not a bug. The actual bug is that lowSamples is incremented even while chiming, so a held button during the chime consumes the confirm and sets armed=false, then on release armed=true — acceptable. No bug here.

reported.title: Chime start latency can exceed 120 ms
reported.description: With POLL_MS=30 and CONFIRM_SAMPLES=2, a press is confirmed after up to ~60 ms of polling plus the delay, and startChime is called in the same loop iteration, so latency is bounded by ~90 ms — within 120 ms. Not a bug.

reported.title: Press during chime is dropped but not counted, and re-arm requires release — matches spec
reported.description: Behaviour says presses while chiming are ignored, which the sketch does. No bug.

truth.description: The button is polled every 30 ms and two consecutive low samples are required, so a 45 ms press is missed unless it happens to cover two samples

judge_input.spec:
- Chime driver on D7; doorbell button on D4 with internal pull-up (active LOW).
- A settled press of at least 40 ms on D4 sounds the chime: D7 HIGH for 300 ms, starting within 120 ms of the press.
- Presses while the chime is sounding are ignored.
- D7 stays LOW whenever no press has been accepted.
- Print `chime n=<count>` every 1000 ms.
